chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: Vocalion session of 4 February 1938
summary: They play 'It's Wonderful', 'Dark Eyes', 'A Brown Bird Sings' and 'You Went to My Head'; Stuff Smith and Gershwin come up.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well you had several recording sessions in 1938 which is when you went out to Hollywood.

Maybe we can move on. Okay, the next session you made was in February of 1938 on the 4th, also recorded in New York like everything else so far. And these are four sides for Vocalion, one of which is a very hard to find item apparently --

And after the playing is over, I want to read into the tape two parenthetical comments. One has to do with an expression that Maxine used, 'Housewifes Parade,' in the United Kingdom. I believed what she was talking about was a program that was broadcast on the BBC's light program weekdays at nine o'clock in the morning. It was a request show for housewives. And the title was 'Housewives' Choice.' The second has to do with the name Mezz

Mezzrow. Quite possibly, what Maxine meant to say was Hugues Panassie who came over to the USA to record Mezz Mezzrow.
This can be checked when the tape is being edited -- when the transcript is being edited by Maxine.

It is hard to get. I haven't been able to locate it myself, but I think that somewhere along the line, somebody may have given me a copy of it. You know, "A Brown Bird Sings" is one of the last -- was the last selections I made for Vocalion. And, of course, on the other side is a selection by the Charioteers. And they have to look under the Charioteers to find the proper singer. But it was always a favorite of mine. And then, of course, "It's Wonderful", was written by Stuff Smith. I think sometimes people get that confused with "S Wonderful" --

Right. But by this time, Stuff had come back to New York, and he came to the club and brought me a copy of this tune that he supposedly had written. His name is on it now. It later turned out that him and somebody else wrote it, and then -- I think Robins published it -- but I introduced it at the Onyx Club. And it became quite a favorite. And, of course, a few years later, I run into Al Cohn who wants to know if I know a song, 'It's Wonderful.' And he hummed a few bars. I said, 'Yeah, I introduced it in 1938.' He might've been pulling my leg but I'm not sure. 'Dark Eyes', these are things that were selected by Claude. I guess he figured that we shouldn't get too far away from the format -- you know, keeping something traditional on the album. And, of course, 'You Went To My Head' was quite a popular tune at the time. I liked it and he brought it to me. We learned it and -- it's
